findings.reason: the plan must state how the record is committed (its own commit, or the ledger's state-write path) rather than assuming a commit that does not occur.
findings.text: §3's write path asserts the reviewed-run promotion commit carries the record ("no new commit is created"), but _COMMITLESS_ROLES lists "review" and the comment at promotion.py:2566 records that a review "promotes without a commit, which is its correct disposition" because a review's deliverable sits outside the repository, so there is no commit for the store write to ride

findings.reason: placement and the commit should extend the ledger owner, not fork a second writer of the same committed tree, which is how the review record and the run ledger would drift.
findings.text: §3 adds docs/state/<project>/reviews/<...>.json and a writer that commits it, but reckon/ledger.py owns the committed state tree (docs/state/<project>/ via ledger_path/run_path) and the commit of a state write (_commit_state_write), and the plan never names it

findings.reason: the section must account for the added public surface in its own text, per the interface-budget rule.
findings.text: §3 adds a server route GET /review/<project>/<id> and a new MCP surface for the record by id, and names nothing the change retires or merges or why nothing can be

findings.reason: the section must name the view it merges or retires, or state why the payload cannot extend an existing view (e.g. the existing crew(view="plan-review")), before adding a view.
findings.text: §4 adds "a crew view reporting, per plan and per day, the reviews run, the authored-prose change behind each re-review and how often §22's threshold fired", a new member of the mcp_views family (33), and the only thing it names as replaced is the throwaway scripts edit_size.py/section_change.py, which are not a counted family

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the committed store plus one reader (extending read_plan_review/list_plan_reviews) hides record shape, path resolution and the join behind a few functions rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 places a committed store at docs/state/<project>/reviews/ and moves it through a promotion commit, but reckon/ledger.py owns placement under docs/state/<project>/ and the state-write commit.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4 adds a crew view to the mcp_views family and §3 adds a server route and MCP surface, and neither section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 cites "The review run's own promotion commit moves the record into the committed store, so no new commit is created", but a review run is a commitless role and promotes without a commit, so the cited carrier does not exist.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every added layer is justified as an extension of an existing mechanism: §3 changes where store_delivered_report writes, §6 extends _review_dispatch_fields, §7 uses the existing set op, §2 is prompt text only.
